title: Global Connections
scope: A selective Indian-city comparison, not a ranking or exhaustive active-partnership census.

cities.extent: 1 formal relationship verified in this review
cities.evidence: Cupertino records a November 2012 MoU and describes a community nonprofit supporting arts, student programmes and visits.
cities.lesson: Build with the existing community bridge. Ask what help would make its next project useful to both cities.
cities.limit: Bloemfontein is kept separately as a reported 2017 proposal. This is a verified minimum, not a complete municipal register.

cities.partners: Examples include Los Angeles, Yokohama, Stuttgart and Shanghai
cities.evidence: The 2025 municipal yearbook names Los Angeles, then 16 further relationships. It illustrates a much broader recorded network.
cities.lesson: Give relationships a durable administrative home and preserve the agreement history.
cities.limit: A count of names in a historical roster, not 17 programmes confirmed active today. The source uses some historic city and country names.

cities.extent: At least 3 documented partners in this sample
cities.evidence: Denver describes student exchanges and Taste of India; San Antonio connects its annual Diwali festival to the relationship. MEA records the Chongqing agreement.
cities.lesson: Let culture create a recurring public meeting point, and connect it to learning.
cities.limit: Three individually documented examples, not Chennai’s total. Described programmes do not establish their current scale or impact.

cities.evidence: The SF–Bangalore initiative describes a citizen-diplomacy organisation with committees spanning culture, entrepreneurship, health and urban services.
cities.lesson: A civic organisation can bring people and institutions together around specific subjects.
cities.limit: This row examines one relationship; it does not count all Bengaluru partners. Published committee descriptions are not verified current outcomes.

cities.extent: At least 3 named foreign municipal partners
cities.evidence: Brisbane records a 2010 tripartite agreement with Ipswich and Hyderabad. MEA records a separate Hyderabad–Qingdao agreement in 2015.
cities.lesson: A collaboration can involve more than two cities when their institutions have a shared purpose.
cities.limit: Brisbane and Ipswich count as two municipalities in one agreement. Current programme activity has not been audited.

cities.evidence: Bremen’s 2021 official statement discusses its long-standing cooperation with Pune and wider academic links with India.
cities.lesson: People, universities and civic groups can sustain a relationship beyond an announcement.
cities.limit: A dated cooperation example, not a total or a claim of a currently active exchange. Do not equate every friendship with a formal sister-city agreement.
